URL: https://www.irishtimes.com/world/europe/2026/07/24/wildfires-spain-declares-national-emergency-as-france-seeks-eu-help/
(Search snippet content — Irish Times / France & Spain wildfire reporting, 24 July 2026)

Over 166,000 people evacuated in France and Spain as forest fires raged near Madrid and Bordeaux. At least 141,000 evacuated in southwestern France and 25,000 in the Madrid region, among them more than 1,200 elderly and disabled people.
Spain declared a national emergency in two regions, military units leading efforts; merged fires near Madrid and Avila displaced or confined 60,000 people.
French President Emmanuel Macron on Friday asked the army to mobilise to help contain the worst wildfire the country has ever seen after seeking European Union help.
Some 44,000 people fled the Cap Ferret peninsula south of Bordeaux; the main blaze near Cap Ferret (60km from Bordeaux), active since Wednesday, has consumed 125 square kilometres.
Temperatures topped 40C (104F).

URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/23/spain-and-france-battle-raging-wildfires-face-high-risk-of-more
This summer has burned the second-largest area on record across the European Union; a third heatwave has driven one of the EU's worst wildfire seasons on record. EU reinforcements: Croatian and Portuguese firefighting aircraft, helicopters from Czech Republic and Slovakia to France; Italy and Greece each sending two Canadair water-dumping planes to Spain.
